title: Hiroyuki Sanada in Final Talks for Hiruzen Sarutobi in Naruto Movie
excerpt:
The Shōgun star is negotiating to play the Third Hokage.
His participation has not yet been announced as a completed deal.
body_md:
Hiroyuki Sanada is in final negotiations to join Lionsgate's live-action Naruto film as Hiruzen Sarutobi, according to an exclusive report from Deadline. The Shōgun actor would portray the Third Hokage, one of the Hidden Leaf Village's most respected leaders. The wording matters: negotiations are advanced, but the report does not establish that a contract has been signed or that the studio has formally confirmed his casting.

Hiruzen Sarutobi is a major figure in Masashi Kishimoto's manga and its anime adaptations. Known in his youth as the God of Shinobi, he is remembered for his exceptional abilities and his sense of responsibility toward Konoha. His compassion frequently conflicts with the difficult choices required of a village leader. His faith in the next generation of ninja is central to his character.

Sanada brings a long career in Japanese and international film and television. In addition to his acclaimed performance in Shōgun, his credits include John Wick: Chapter 4, Bullet Train and Mortal Kombat. He is also a trained martial artist and karate black belt, qualities that make him a compelling potential choice for a legendary ninja leader. Nevertheless, his involvement should continue to be described as reported talks until a formal announcement is made.

Destin Daniel Cretton is attached to write and direct the adaptation. The filmmaker previously directed Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings. Avi Arad, Ari Arad and Emmy Yu are producing for Arad Productions, while Cretton and Jeyun Munford are involved through Hisako. The report also says Charles Melton is in talks for a role, without presenting that negotiation as a finalized casting announcement.

Naruto follows the energetic young Naruto Uzumaki, who dreams of becoming the leader of his ninja village while carrying the spirit of a nine-tailed fox inside him. Kishimoto's manga ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 1999 to 2014, becoming an international phenomenon with more than 250 million copies in print across over 60 countries and territories. The franchise subsequently expanded through successful animated series and other media.

The live-action film faces high expectations, especially regarding casting, visual effects and the translation of the manga's world into live action. Sanada's potential participation is a significant development, but the distinction between negotiations and a confirmed deal remains essential. The report does not provide an official theatrical release date.
